text: The swarm starts soon. Read swarm/GOAL.md and swarm/README.md on integration.

Checks for P01 P02 P03 P08 P10 P13 are on integration. Run npm run milestones. GOAL.md now says: every command (measure, guards, proposer, run, compare) runs in the problem folder inside the scratch checkout, and every path is relative to the problem folder. P13 now needs P16.

Checks for P04 P05 P06 P07 P11 P12 are on integration too: 12 of 17 milestones now have checks. GOAL.md adds a top-level 'candidates' field (default 1), says two runs are the same problem when they have the same name in the same repository, and says '-20' is -20.

GOAL.md: an exact measure (same number on every run, runs can be 1) keeps any change in the right direction. The decision rule must handle this; a rank test alone cannot. Noisy measures still need a statistical test.

STAGE 2 is open: swarm/GOAL-2.md and milestones S01-S05 in swarm/milestones.json (Anthropic provider for solve, cost in result.json with budget.max_usd, solve --resume, measure draft, Synthe solving itself). Their checks come in about 1-2 hours. Free helpers: build to GOAL-2.md now; stage 1 work (P09 P14 P15 P16 FINAL) still comes first. Also new and frozen: scripts/score/ and swarm/hidden/ (the scorer and an encrypted hidden problem set). Never try to read, decrypt or tune to swarm/hidden/.

ALL STAGE 1 CHECKS ARE ON INTEGRATION: P09 P14 P15 P16 FINAL and the zoo in swarm/zoo/ (12 problems). Run npm run milestones. P16: the model reply content is the proposer stdout object {"proposals": [...]}. A holdout win means strictly better. FINAL has a 300 s limit and puts one seed's problem in a subfolder. swarm/zoo/ is frozen: never special-case it.

COORDINATOR RULING on judge length control (P09): remove padTo / the lorem-ipsum padding from src/solve/judge.ts. It fits the check's fake judge (exact character counts, no trailing space because that judge trims) and would hurt a real model judge, which reads filler as a worse reply. Tomorrow the Synthe score runs with a real Claude judge, so this matters. The check author showed the plain rule passes P09 with margin: ask every comparison in both orders, then a one-sided paired sign test over cases (real gain kept 99.99%, length trap 0.03%). If you want length control, make it statistical (for example, report the length difference, or require the win to hold on cases where the change is not longer), never by changing the texts the judge reads. lead: assign one PR for this on top of #139; keep P09 and FINAL passing.

P09 CHECK UPDATED (frozen): the judge must see exactly the outputs that run printed. padTo now fails P09. Remove the padding step in src/solve/judge.ts (the second askTwice pass on padded text); the two-order paired test alone passed the new P09 3 of 3 times on #139's branch. GOAL.md says it too.

STAGE 2 CHECKS ARE ON INTEGRATION: S01-S05 (helpers-s.ts). S05 passes today; keep it passing. S01-S04 fail for the right reasons: no model.provider/prices, no budget.max_usd, no cost in result.json, --resume ignored, no measure command. Note: S01 and S02 also need judged measures in solve. GOAL-2.md adds measure.judge.rubric for compare "model", and says output a comes before b in the judge request. Stage 1 still comes first.

Three tasks from the monitor's review are in the task list, and they come before new features: a holdout leak through failure reasons (P07), a key forwarded to compare commands (S01), and max_usd passed by parallel judge calls (S02). The real scoring run depends on all three.

Ruling on mon's #147 doubt: keep it. A file that the measure reads may be edited only when artifact names it exactly; that is the person's explicit choice (for example, a config that is both tuned and scored). problem check must warn about it in plain words: task coordinator-4. h05 takes it as its last task, then stops.
